Driving the real apps — your core instruction — was the whole difference. It exposed **seven** latent bugs that every unit test and CI check stayed green through: iOS not linking the Rust core, the library-search-path, the Android JNI crash, the flatc version mismatch, the account-reversion (NMP#2932), the projection_rev/host-cache defect that was the empty-feed root cause (NMP#2944/#2952), and the unimplemented `nativeResolveRef` JNI wrappers that only fired once a card finally rendered. Each is fixed. I over-claimed "done" several times during the chase and had to walk it back — the honest bar turned out to be exactly the one you set: a feed rendering in a real app, not a green test suite.

Remaining tails, all tracked, none blocking: chirp#46 (cosmetic display-name resolution), chirp#32/#35/#36 (fuller platform surface), the publish-gated web items, and the NMP findings filed along the way (#2918, #2926, #2930, #2943→dup). The only thing genuinely in your court is the rc.2 publish ownership. [...] 
So the straight answer to "does the collapse work end-to-end on a real device": **not yet demonstrated — and there's a credible framework-side reason it doesn't.** This is precisely the payoff of your "actually drive the apps" instruction: the unit and engine tests were all green while the real app shows an empty feed, and driving it exposed a gap nothing else did.
